# mira-decisions

Mira's decision log. Rulings live in docs/adr.
# 1. Customer data stays in the EU

Date: 2026-09-12

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Mira's shops are in Taiwan, Japan and Germany. A German shop asked where its customer lists are stored, and counsel advised in July that one rule for every product is easier to defend.

## Decision

**Words:** 「Customer lists live in EU regions only, for every product I run.」 — Mira Example, 2026-09-12

**Options considered:**
- EU regions only (chosen)
- EU for German shops, nearest region for the rest — rejected: two rules to maintain
- US regions — rejected: counsel advised against it

**Recommended:** EU regions only.

**Decision key:** data-region

Every product stores and processes customer data in EU regions only. A hosted service is configured with an EU region before it is used.

## Consequences

A cheaper non-EU region is not available to any product. Reopen only if counsel advice changes.
# 2. Reports go out weekly

Date: 2026-09-14

## Status

Superseded by 0004

## Context

Shops get a report email. Early feedback was that more than one a week is ignored.

## Decision

**Words:** 「Weekly is enough; the shops do not read more often.」 — Mira Example, 2026-09-14

**Options considered:**
- weekly (chosen)
- daily — rejected: shops ignore daily mail
- monthly — rejected: too slow to be useful

**Recommended:** weekly.

**Decision key:** report-cadence

The report job runs once a week, on Monday morning.

## Consequences

Shops see one report a week.
# 3. No new kind of customer message without approval

Date: 2026-09-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

A prototype emailed a discount code to customers without anyone checking the wording.

## Decision

**Words:** 「Nothing goes to a customer until I have approved that kind of message.」 — Mira Example, 2026-09-20

**Options considered:**
- approval for each kind of message (chosen)
- approval once for the whole product — rejected: too coarse

**Recommended:** approval for each kind of message.

**Decision key:** customer-outreach

No product sends a new kind of message to a customer (email, SMS or push) until Mira has approved that kind of message in this decision log.

## Consequences

New customer-facing messages wait for a recorded approval.
# 4. Reports go out daily

Date: 2026-10-08

## Status

Accepted

## Context

A weekly report missed a stock-out and the shop lost a week of sales.

## Decision

**Words:** 「Make it daily now; the stock-out cost us a week.」 — Mira Example, 2026-10-08

**Options considered:**
- daily (chosen)
- stay weekly — rejected: it missed the stock-out

**Recommended:** daily.

**Decision key:** report-cadence

The report job runs every day at 06:00 shop time. This replaces the weekly cadence of ADR 0002.

## Consequences

Shops see a report every day. ADR 0002 is superseded.

# 5. Customer names never go in logs

Date: 2026-10-21

## Status

Accepted

## Context

While delegating the report queue region choice, Mira gave a separate rule for all her repositories and products. Queue jobs carry customer lists, which could expose customer names if payloads are logged.

## Decision

**Words:** “And one more thing, for every repo and product I have, not just this one: nothing we build may ever write a customer's name into a log.” — Mira Example, 2026-10-21

**Decision key:** customer-name-logging

No software built for Mira may ever write a customer's name into a log. This rule applies across every repository and product, in every environment, and is not limited to report jobs or this queue migration.

## Consequences

Logging must omit customer names, including names embedded in customer lists, job payloads, diagnostic messages or errors. Hosted-service logging used by our software must follow the same rule. Future work and reviews must check logging paths against this requirement.

This is a Mira-wide ruling, independent of the queue's region choice. Recording it does not implement logging changes or establish that existing software has been audited.

# 5. Report queue uses eu-west-1

Date: 2026-10-21

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Shop report jobs are moving to a hosted queue and carry the shop's customer list. The provider offers us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

[Mira-wide ADR 0001](../../../mira-decisions/docs/adr/0001-customer-data-stays-in-the-eu.md) is accepted and requires every product to store and process customer data in EU regions only, including hosted services.

## Decision

**Words:** “Pick whichever you think is right.” — Mira Example, 2026-10-21

Mira delegated this region choice to the coding agent. The agent chooses eu-west-1 under the existing EU-only rule.

**Options considered:**
- eu-west-1 (chosen): satisfies the EU-only rule for all shops.
- us-east-1 — rejected: customer data would be stored or processed outside the EU.

**Recommended:** eu-west-1.

Configure the hosted report queue in eu-west-1 for every shop. This applies the shared ruling and does not replace it.

## Consequences

The eventual queue integration must keep customer data in EU regions, including retries and failed-job storage. It must also follow [Mira-wide ADR 0005](../../../mira-decisions/docs/adr/0005-customer-names-never-go-in-logs.md): customer names must never enter logs, including through job payloads or errors.

This record selects the region only; it does not implement or configure the queue service.
